title: Foreign Minister Lin attends opening of TECO in Phoenix
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung attended the opening of the Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) in Phoenix on October 5. The ceremony was attended by over 200 political figures, community leaders from Taiwan and the United States, and representatives of Taiwan’s industries including TSMC. Among the guests were TECO in Phoenix Director General Kevin Chiao, Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs, Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego, US Representative Andy Biggs, and American Institute in Taiwan Managing Director Ingrid Larson.

In remarks at the event, Minister Lin said that a new milestone had been reached in the mutually beneficial Taiwan-US partnership with the opening of TECO in Phoenix. He added that the model of cooperation between Taiwan and the United States that had been established in Arizona served as an excellent example of how Taiwan-US cooperation was creating mutually beneficial outcomes.

Prior to the ceremony, Minister Lin held separate meetings with Governor Hobbs and Mayor Gallego, during which he affirmed the long-standing efforts of Arizona and Phoenix to support the development of Taiwan’s enterprises in the state. Discussions also delved into issues of two-way investment, talent development, and technological and industrial cooperation. Following the meetings, Minister Lin and Governor Hobbs jointly witnessed the signing of an MOU on cooperation between Taiwan’s National Innovation and Entrepreneurship Association (NIEA) and the Arizona Commerce Authority (ACA). The agreement will promote the integration of Taiwanese enterprises into the Arizona market and connect them to investment opportunities and industrial resources. It will also enhance cooperation between Taiwan’s companies and local US governments.

Minister Lin also visited the TSMC Arizona facility to better understand the development of Taiwan’s enterprises and the formation of industrial clusters in Arizona. Here, he held a discussion with firms in TSMC’s supply chain. Minister Lin also led a business delegation to the ACA for a briefing on the investment environment in Arizona, visited the Halo Vista Industrial Park adjacent to the TSMC campus, and toured the Arizona State University (ASU) Polytechnic Innovation Zone to better understand the needs of Taiwanese firms as concerns investment, operations, and long-term development in the United States.

TECO in Phoenix is Taiwan’s fourteenth office in the United States. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to leverage the office to enhance cooperation with various sectors in Arizona and New Mexico, working with enterprises and drawing on Taiwan’s strengths to expand trade, technology, and personnel exchanges with the United States. These efforts will benefit Taiwan’s people and, through collaboration with US partners, create a resilient global supply chain network.
